title: From First Orbit to Moon
question: How did a Cold War rivalry take people from a single orbit to the Moon?
hook: Two rival nations raced to send people up, and one of them ended up walking on the Moon.
idea: Missile programs gave two rival nations rockets big enough for space, and the race between them carried people from first flights to six Moon landings.

beats.prompt: Put these early firsts in order.
items: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space
Alan Shepard becomes the first American in space
John Glenn becomes the first American in orbit
Valentina Tereshkova becomes the first woman in space
beats.explain: Gagarin flew on 12 April 1961, Shepard on 5 May 1961, Glenn on 20 February 1962, and Tereshkova on 16 June 1963.

beats.prompt: The USSR stretched its one-person Vostok capsule into the Voskhod to rival Gemini, and won the first spacewalk. What happened to the Voskhod program?

choices.label: It went on to land crews on the Moon
choices.feedback: The Soviets did chase the Moon, but with the Soyuz spacecraft, not the Voskhod.

choices.label: It was terminated, because it could not maneuver in orbit like Gemini
It beat Gemini to the first rendezvous and docking
choices.feedback: Winning the spacewalk makes this tempting, but the US Gemini flights performed the first space rendezvous and docking.

beats.explain: Voskhod lacked Gemini's ability to maneuver in orbit, so the program was terminated.

beats.prompt: Match each program to what it did.
pairs: Carried Gagarin on the first human spaceflight
Sent Alan Shepard on the first American spaceflight
Made the first space rendezvous and docking
Put 12 men on the Moon in six landings
beats.explain: Each program was a step from the first human flights toward the Moon.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: The US and the Soviet Union built intercontinental ballistic missiles to deliver nuclear weapons.
Those missiles were far too small to lift anything into orbit.
So spaceflight had to be developed using different rockets entirely.
Yet the Soviet Union launched the first satellites in 1957 and 1958.
beats.explain: The missiles produced rockets large enough to be adapted to carry the first artificial satellites into low Earth orbit.
